title: Roadmap Linkage Map & Timebox-Gated Handoff Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a lightweight, actionable system to make cross-team roadmap dependencies visible, measurable, and automatable across Eng / Design / Security / Infra. The deliverable is a Roadmap Linkage Map (RLM) plus an accompanying Timebox-Gated Handoff Protocol (TGHP) that: 1) surfaces dependency owners and critical path; 2) enforces gated handoff checkpoints tied to cycle milestones; and 3) wires alerts into the Console/OKR dashboards and Linear to reduce manual coordination overhead.

Why this matters:
- We continue to see last-minute blockers during rollouts where a security review or infra change slips and delays the entire release.
- PMs currently maintain ad-hoc spreadsheets and Slack threads; this creates hidden technical debt and missed OKR targets.
- A small amount of automation and clearer handoff contract should reduce cross-team unblock time and improve roadmap predictability.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce cross-team unblock median time by 30% for Q1 rollouts (baseline tracking starts when a dependency is flagged).
- Increase visibility: 95% of roadmap tickets with external dependencies should have an RLM entry and assigned owner.
- Reduce last-minute gating incidents (post-code-complete block on shipping) by 50% over 3 cycles.

Proposal (high level):
1) Roadmap Linkage Map (RLM):
   - A canonical lightweight record per dependency containing: dependent ticket key, dependent team, dependency type (design review, infra changes, security signoff, capacity), owner, handoff window, and risk rating.
   - Implement RLM as an augmented metadata record attached to Linear tickets + mirrored rows in a shared Confluence page for exec views.
2) Timebox-Gated Handoff Protocol (TGHP):
   - Define gate checkpoints relative to cycle milestones (e.g., design-review by cycle start+1 week, security signoff by cycle start+3 weeks).
   - Each gate has explicit acceptance criteria and a fallback plan (e.g., ship with disabled feature flag + post-launch remediation).
3) Automation & Signals:
   - Linear automation: when a dependency is added, create a subtask in the dependency owner’s queue and set a gating deadline.
   - Console wiring: a new dashboard card that surfaces outstanding RLM entries and their risk scores; alerts for gates at T-72h and T-24h before deadline.
   - GitHub integration: automatically attach PR links and CI status to RLM entries for engineering dependencies.
4) OKR linkage and reporting:
   - Map RLM entries to initiative/OKR tags so we can attribute missed OKR milestones to specific cross-team breaks.

Acceptance criteria (must have):
- RLM schema documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Roadmap+Linkage+Map (prototype page).
- Linear template for adding RLM metadata to tickets and automation rule created (see automation PR).
- Console dashboard prototype that lists outstanding RLM items and risk levels; alerts firing in test workspace.
- Pilot run with 3 active initiatives (one infra-heavy, one runtime/serving, one console UX) across at least Eng, Design, and Security.

Non-goals:
- Not building a full dependency management product. This is an operational layer + signals to reduce manual coordination.

Trade-offs & design considerations:
- Lightweight vs authoritative: aim for minimal friction (prefill owners from CODEOWNERS / design lead) rather than forcing strict enforcement that slows teams.
- Risk scoring: start with heuristic scoring (impact x likelihood) to avoid complex models initially.
- Automation scope: prefer Linear + Console + GitHub integrations first; postpone Slack bot and email escalation until we validate signal value.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): final RLM schema, Confluence page, Linear ticket template, and automation rule spec.
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): Linear automation, basic Console dashboard, GitHub PR attach integration, pilot with runtime-1.18 and console-2025.12 initiatives.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): expand pilot, add OKR mapping, refine gate thresholds, collect metrics.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): onboarding docs, retro, and rollout to broader org.

Metrics & instrumentation:
- Metric 1: median unblock interval (time from dependency flagged -> owner acknowledges / takes action).
- Metric 2: % of roadmap tickets with filled RLM entries.
- Metric 3: number of last-minute gating incidents (post-code-complete blocks).
- Dashboards: Console card + weekly emailed digest for PM leads.

Risks & mitigation:
- Low adoption: mitigate with prefilled owners and minimal required fields.
- Incorrect owners: add a mandatory owner-confirm step triggered by automation.
- Noise from low-value dependencies: add a minimum impact threshold and allow triage to mark as low-priority.

Pilot candidates (initial):

- console-2025.12 UX revamp (ENG-24401, DES-8101)
- dedicated-autoscale policy (INF-1132, ENG-24900)

Rollout plan & success criteria:
- Pilot completion with at least 3 initiatives and confirmation of metrics collection (by 2026-01-15).
- Post-pilot retrospective and decision on expanding to org-wide mandatory RLM for initiatives > P2 priority.
